title: Vito resolved and survived — tutor for the second piece, or hold?

board.you: Turn 8, precombat main, 24 life. Battlefield: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose (cast after combat last turn — he has survived one full table rotation), Black Market Connections, Nighthawk Scavenger (flying, deathtouch, lifelink), Legion Lieutenant, three 1/1 Vampire tokens, eight lands, all untapped. Edgar Markov is still in the command zone.
board.table: Player 2 (Azorius control) is at 30 with FIVE untapped lands and has held instant-speed mana every turn; they killed your Sanctum Seeker on sight two turns ago. Player 3 (Rakdos midrange) is at 18 and tapped out rebuilding from their own losses. Player 4 (Selesnya enchantress engine) is at 36 and drew three extra cards last rotation. Everyone at this bracket-4 table knows what Vito means — he survived the rotation because killing a lone Vito felt wasteful, not because anyone forgot.

scenario.mana_available: 8 (all lands untapped; Black Market Connections' costs are paid on resolution of its trigger)
stack: Black Market Connections trigger (beginning of your precombat main phase) — you will choose modes on resolution; life paid here is YOUR loss and does not seed the Vito loop
scenario.extras: The two tutorable halves differ in kind: Exquisite Blood ({4}{B}, enchantment — stack 001's loop, verified as a deterministic 38-iteration full-table kill from a 2-life seed, each Vito trigger freshly targeted, the killing loss still triggering the chain) versus Bloodthirsty Conqueror ({3}{B}{B}, creature — stack 004's loop, verified equally unbounded in 13 iterations but with a named removal window every iteration because the gain half is a creature). Demonic Tutor + Exquisite Blood is 7 of your 8 mana in one turn; Nighthawk Scavenger's lifelink on any connect seeds either loop. Both verified kills assumed the loop went unopposed — stack 001's scenario stated opponents held no instant-speed interaction.
scenario.question: Do you Demonic Tutor now and present the kill this turn into Player 2's five open mana, tutor now but hold the piece as hidden information, or keep the tutor itself flexible and win another way?

branches.choice: Tutor for Exquisite Blood and present the kill now
branches.line: Resolve Black Market Connections (take the card, pay the life). Demonic Tutor for Exquisite Blood, cast it (7 mana total), then attack with Nighthawk Scavenger; one point of lifelink connection triggers Vito, and the loop is live: verified stack 001 says it is deterministic and unbounded — 38 iterations killed a 75-life table from a 2-life seed, retargeting each trigger, with even the killing blow's loss re-feeding the chain.
branches.signals: Demonic Tutor with Vito on board is a fire alarm; casting a five-mana enchantment immediately after is the fire. Player 2 has held five mana all game and killed your last engine piece on sight — you are presenting lethal into the one player whose whole posture says 'I have the answer.'
branches.coalition_risk: Total. A presented infinite unites all three opponents instantly, and unlike the combat plan there is no partial credit: if the loop is broken you have spent your best tutor, seven mana, and every scrap of goodwill for an enchantment that reads 'kill my Vito next.'
branches.coaching: Understand exactly where this line loses: not to enchantment removal, but to a kill spell on Vito. Every iteration of the loop is a triggered ability that goes on the stack and passes priority — 'Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that's not a card the next time a player would receive priority' — so Player 2 gets a window before the first Vito trigger resolves, and Vito dying mid-loop ends it (your gain continues off Exquisite Blood; the conversion to their loss is gone). Stack 001's table-kill is a fact about the loop, not about this table: its scenario stipulated no instant-speed interaction held, and Player 2's five lands are the negation of that premise. The pivot-window rule is written for exactly this moment: 'assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing.' Five open mana from a proven interaction deck fails that count. This branch is correct in a different scenario — Player 2 tapped out, or Deflecting Swat castable for free because Edgar is on the battlefield — and naming those preconditions is the point of rejecting it today.

citations.quote: Once an ability has triggered, its controller puts it on the stack as an object that’s not a card the next time a player would receive priority.
assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing
If a player has 0 or less life, that player loses the game.

branches.choice: Tutor now, hold the piece hidden; complete it in a dead window
branches.line: Resolve Black Market Connections. Demonic Tutor for Exquisite Blood and put it in your hand — hidden information. Spend the remaining six mana on unremarkable development: a Vampire or two (each banks an eminence token) while keeping the board's silhouette boring. Cast Exquisite Blood on the first turn Player 2 is tapped to two or fewer or has just spent their wrath, then seed the loop with any lifelink connect.
branches.signals: The tutor itself telegraphs — everyone assumes you went for a combo piece — but an assumption is not a target. The tutored card cannot be answered in your hand, and the table's fear now works FOR you: Player 2 must respect the threat every turn, which taxes their mana on defense against a card you choose when to reveal. Expect Vito to eat a removal spell soon; that is a fine trade.
branches.coalition_risk: Moderate and manageable. You are scarier in the abstract but present nothing to unite against. If Vito dies to the panic you induced, they spent a card killing the {2}{B} half — the recastable half — while the seven-mana half stays hidden.
branches.coaching: This is threat-deflection played with real cards: 'sequence scary pieces after the table's removal is spent.' The asymmetry between the halves is your whole plan — Vito is cheap, recastable, and already the oldest news on the board; Exquisite Blood is expensive, an enchantment (immune to the creature removal and wraths this table is actually holding), and invisible until the turn it wins. Compare the loops you could have fetched: stack 004 verified Conqueror + Vito kills identically (13 iterations, exact-lethal arithmetic) but names a removal window every iteration because the gain half is a creature — fetch Conqueror only when you need a blocker or when 'can't gain life' hate is on the board and you want the deathtouch body regardless. The discipline this line demands is patience under a clock: the goldfish says natural assembly was never coming (2.8% by turn 6, 4.9% by turn 10) — the tutor IS the assembly — and Player 4's enchantress engine is compounding, so 'a dead window' means the next two or three turns, not someday. Name your trigger now: Player 2 taps for their draw engine or wraths, and you combo through the gap that same turn.

citations.quote: sequence scary pieces after the table's removal is spent
protection up, table tapped out, interaction counted and accounted for

branches.choice: Hold the tutor entirely; keep winning with the board
branches.line: Resolve Black Market Connections, keep Demonic Tutor in hand as a flexible answer (it can fetch Despark or Fracture for Player 4's enchantress engine, Teferi's Protection against a wrath, or the combo half later), and spend the turn on the go-wide plan: cast Vampires, bank eminence tokens, and pressure Player 3's open life total.
branches.signals: Quietest line — the table sees a typal deck durdling and the spotlight drifts to Player 4's draw engine. But you also spend a turn NOT converting the one card in your hand that turns your 3% lategame into a certainty.
branches.coalition_risk: Lowest today. The cost is paid to the clock instead: the strategic frame's metagame-clock warning is that four-player games trend long and inevitability compounds toward engines — Player 4's, not yours.
branches.coaching: The frame calls the infinite 'tutor-backed lategame insurance, not plan A,' and this branch takes that literally — sometimes correctly. The test is whether your combat plan is actually winning: here it is not. Sanctum Seeker is dead, so the each-opponent drain engine that makes go-wide combat scale against ~120 combined life is offline; mean bodies by turn 10 is 6.36, and six bodies of fair damage split across three opponents beats nobody before the enchantress deck goes over the top. Holding Demonic as an answer is real optionality — but audit what you would actually fetch: if the honest answer is 'Exquisite Blood, next turn, when it feels safer,' you are paying a full turn for the feeling, and Branch B buys the same safety today with the piece already secured. Take this branch when the board genuinely wins without the combo (Sanctum alive, Bloodletter drawn) or when a known hate piece blanks the loop and the tutor must become removal. Neither is true on this board.

citations.quote: don't overextend into an unknown sweeper without a reason

recommendation.choice: Tutor now, hold the piece hidden; complete it in a dead window
recommendation.rationale: The tutor converts a 4.9%-by-turn-10 natural assembly into a certainty, so casting it is nearly free equity — the entire decision is WHEN the second half becomes public, and hidden zones are the only place a bracket-4 table cannot interact with your combo. Branch A fails the open-mana count (five held lands from the player who has answered your engines on sight, with every loop iteration offering a priority window on Vito — 603.3, and stack 004's named weakness), while Branch C donates a turn to the enchantress engine that owns the long game, holding a tutor whose best fetch you already know. Branch B keeps every threat live at once: the table must respect combat, eminence keeps banking bodies, Vito baits removal at a one-mana-for-one-card exchange rate you happily accept, and Exquisite Blood — the enchantment half, immune to the creature interaction this table is actually holding — resolves the turn Player 2 taps out or wraths. Telegraphed is not the same as answerable. Make them play against a card they cannot see, and present the verified 38-iteration kill (stack 001) only in the window where its one prerequisite — Vito surviving a single priority pass — is something you control.
